about.text: Lactulose is a non-absorbable sugar used in the treatment of constipation and hepatic encephalopathy. It is administered orally for constipation, and either orally or rectally for hepatic encephalopathy. It generally begins working after 8–12 hours, but may take up to 2 days to improve constipation.

how.text: Lactulose is not in milk: it is made from lactose, often from whey lactose, by warming a lactose solution with an alkaline catalyst until part of it rearranges. The syrup is then purified; a crystalline product is made by crystallising it.

steps.name: rearrange
steps.note: Warmed with an alkaline catalyst (NaOH, Na₂CO₃, (NH₄)₂CO₃ or sodium aluminate, borate also used) for minutes to a few hours, so the glucose half of lactose becomes fructose.

facts.v: Lobry de Bruyn–Alberda van Ekenstein rearrangement
Plain alkali gives under about 30 % lactulose; sodium aluminate can reach 80–85 % yield at 55–65 % lactose conversion
Galactose, epilactose, tagatose, and acids (isosaccharinic, formic); they limit the yield and must be purified away
Higher pH, temperature or time makes lactose and lactulose degrade
Enzymatic routes (cellobiose 2-epimerase, β-galactosidase) are being developed, not the main industrial route
